# How to use this editorial

Recover the geometric invariant and degeneracy policy before comparing code.

# A. Orthogonal Crossings

## How to find it

Sweeping by x turns every horizontal into an active interval in time and every vertical into a y-range query. Write the endpoint convention before selecting the add/query/remove order.

## Derivation and correctness

At sweep coordinate x, the Fenwick tree contains exactly horizontals whose closed x-range contains x because adds precede queries and removals follow them. A vertical query sums exactly active y-values in its closed interval. Total time is `O((H+V) log(H+V))`.

## Failure-focused tests

Compare with the independent tiny brute-force oracle. Include collinearity, duplicates, equal event coordinates, boundary contact, and the smallest legal instance.

# B. Rectangle Union

## How to find it

Do not attempt inclusion-exclusion over rectangles. Sweep between consecutive vertical sides; the only changing quantity is the one-dimensional union length on y.

## Derivation and correctness

The active rectangle set changes only at vertical sides. Between event x-values, covered y-length is constant, so multiplying it by the width is exact. The cover-count segment tree stores the union length of active y-intervals. Complexity is `O(n log n)`.

# C. Closest Pair

## How to find it

The slow pair search becomes useful after splitting by x: recursive answers eliminate everything except a narrow cross-boundary strip. The remaining question is why y-order plus packing makes that strip linear.

## Derivation and correctness

A better cross-half pair must lie inside the width-sqrt(d) strip. Sorting it by y permits stopping once the y-gap reaches sqrt(d); planar packing bounds the remaining comparisons per point by a constant. Merging y-orders at every recursion gives `O(n log n)`.

# D. Rectangle Union Perimeter

## Why covered length is insufficient

Problem B's covered y-length gives area, but horizontal perimeter depends on
how many disjoint covered y-components exist. Each segment-tree node therefore
stores:

```text
cover count
covered length
number of covered components
whether its left and right boundaries are covered
```

If local cover is positive, the node is one fully covered component. Otherwise
merge its children and subtract one component when their touching boundaries
are both covered.

## Sweep accounting

Between consecutive x-coordinates, coverage is constant. For strip width
`dx`, add

```text
area      += covered_length * dx
perimeter += 2 * components * dx.
```

At an event coordinate, vertical boundary equals the length covered on exactly
one side of the sweep. Process all additions before removals and, after each
update, add the absolute change in covered length. Additions measure coverage
new on the right; subsequent removals measure coverage lost from the left
that was not replaced by an addition.

## Correctness proof

**Lemma 1.** The tree root stores the exact active covered length and number of
connected y-components.

**Proof.** A positively covered node is its complete geometric interval and
one component. An uncovered leaf contributes nothing. For an uncovered
internal node, child unions are disjoint except possibly at their shared
endpoint; their component counts add, merging exactly once when both touching
boundaries are covered. Structural induction proves every stored field. QED.

**Lemma 2.** Strip contributions equal all nonvertical boundary and area in
that strip.

**Proof.** Active coverage is constant inside the open strip. Its Cartesian
product with width `dx` has the stated area. Every covered y-component has one
top and one bottom boundary spanning the strip, producing `2*components*dx`.
QED.

**Lemma 3.** Event contributions equal all vertical union boundary at that x.

**Proof.** Vertical boundary is the symmetric difference of covered y-sets
immediately before and after the batch. Adding intervals first accumulates the
measure newly covered after the event. Removing ending intervals afterward
accumulates measure covered before but absent after, while portions replaced
by additions remain covered and cause no decrease. QED.

The three lemmas partition the union's area and boundary, proving both outputs.

## Complexity, mistakes, and tests

There are `2n` events and `O(n)` compressed y-intervals. Sorting costs
`O(n log n)` and every update costs `O(log n)`.

Common mistakes include using compressed index counts as length, omitting the
child-boundary merge, processing removals before additions at the same x, and
adding `2*covered_length` instead of `2*components` per unit width. Test
identical rectangles, shared edges, corner contact, nesting, disjoint pieces,
and several starts and ends at one x.

# Stress testing and carry-forward

The D oracle rasterizes small integer rectangles into unit cells. Area is the
number of occupied cells and perimeter is the number of cell sides adjacent to
an unoccupied cell. The transferable state-design lesson is that covered
length alone loses topology; component count plus endpoint flags is the
smallest extra boundary summary needed here.
